text: Join finished vertices; find answers.

Tarjan's offline LCA answers all LCA queries in one DFS with a DSU, O((n + q) α(n)). When the DFS finishes a vertex, join it to its parent in the DSU. For a query (u, v): when the DFS is at u and v is already finished, LCA(u, v) = find(v), the highest ancestor of v whose subtree the DFS is still inside.
It needs all queries in advance (offline). Binary lifting (进阶篇第9章) is online and easier to reuse; Tarjan is the fastest when there are millions of queries.

Store each query at both ends: whichever end finishes second answers it. Mark done[u] before scanning u's queries so a query (u, u) also works.
One cycle: cut an edge, DP twice.

A pseudotree (基环树) is a connected graph with n vertices and n edges: a tree plus one extra edge, so exactly one cycle. When every vertex has exactly one outgoing edge (a functional graph, "each knight hates one other"), every component is a pseudotree. The standard trick: find the cycle, cut one cycle edge (u, v), and solve a tree problem with u or v forced.

Knights (骑士 P2607): choose a maximum-power set with no hating pair. After cutting the cycle edge (u, v), run the "party" tree DP (进阶篇第16章) twice: once forbidding u, once forbidding v; the better of the two respects the cut edge. Sum over components.

A random functional graph of 8 knights, checked against trying all 2⁸ subsets. Two knights hating each other make a 2-cycle with two parallel edges; edge ids keep them apart. Recursion depth can reach n: use an explicit stack for n = 10⁶.
Finish order, then the reversed graph.

Kosaraju's algorithm finds SCCs with two DFS passes: (1) DFS the graph, recording vertices in order of finishing; (2) DFS the reversed graph, starting from vertices in decreasing finish time; each DFS of pass 2 collects exactly one SCC.

Why it works: the vertex that finishes last lies in a "source" SCC; in the reversed graph nothing leaves that SCC, so pass 2 cannot spill into another one. Tarjan (进阶篇第12章) does it in one pass; Kosaraju is easier to remember and also gives the SCCs in topological order.

Centroid tree; O(log n) ancestors.

Dynamic centroid decomposition (动态点分治 / 点分树): record, for every vertex, its parent in the centroid recursion (第6章). This "centroid tree" has depth O(log n), and every path u–v in the original tree passes through LCAcentroid tree(u, v). So a query about all vertices near u only looks at u's O(log n) centroid ancestors, and an update changes data at those same ancestors.

At each centroid c keep a data structure of its subtree indexed by distance to c (a Fenwick tree), plus a second one indexed by distance to c's centroid parent, to subtract the part counted twice. Each query / update: O(log² n) (震波 P6329: sum of values within distance k, with point updates).
Distances in the centroid tree are not tree distances; always use the original tree distance (precomputed with LCA) between u and each centroid ancestor.
